evidence.claim: Xi Jinping was elected general secretary of the 20th CPC Central Committee and named chairman of the CPC Central Military Commission at the first plenary session on October 23, 2022.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping elected general secretary of CPC Central Committee: communique
evidence.excerpt: Xi Jinping was elected general secretary of the 20th CPC Central Committee and named chairman of the CPC Central Military Commission at the first plenary session on October 23, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official communique naming the posts and the session outcome.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 leadership consolidation, immediately relevant to Xi's authority over national security and the military.
contrary_evidence: This confirms authority, not responsible use of that authority.

evidence.claim: Xi said China must modernize its national security system and capacity, pursue a holistic approach to national security, and treat military, technological, social, and international security as core pillars of state security work.
evidence.title: Xi stresses safeguarding national security, social stability
evidence.excerpt: Xi said China must modernize its national security system and capacity, pursue a holistic approach to national security, and treat military, technological, social, and international security as core pillars of state security work.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct speech text from the 20th Party Congress opening session.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent for late-2022 posture and leadership framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for Xi's strategic framing; indirect for downstream implementation.
contrary_evidence: Security-centralizing language can support control and escalation as well as safety.

evidence.claim: The five nuclear-weapon states said a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, that nuclear weapons should serve defensive purposes, and that none of their nuclear weapons are targeted at each other or at any other state.
evidence.title: JOINT STATEMENT Of the Leaders of the Five Nuclear-Weapon States On Preventing Nuclear War and Avoiding Arms Races
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: The five nuclear-weapon states said a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, that nuclear weapons should serve defensive purposes, and that none of their nuclear weapons are targeted at each other or at any other state.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous government text for the five-power statement.
evidence.period_fit: Strong 2022 fit; this is the central public non-escalation statement Xi's China joined.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the level of Chinese head-of-state/party leadership; the statement is joint and system-level.
contrary_evidence: The statement is declaratory and does not itself show later restraint in force structure or crisis behavior.

evidence.claim: China called for continued strategic-stability communication and in-depth dialogue on reducing the role of nuclear weapons in national security doctrines, including on missile defense, outer space, cyberspace, and artificial intelligence.
evidence.title: Upholding the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons for World Peace and Development
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China called for continued strategic-stability communication and in-depth dialogue on reducing the role of nuclear weapons in national security doctrines, including on missile defense, outer space, cyberspace, and artificial intelligence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official NPT review-cycle statement with specific policy asks and issue areas.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 NPT review diplomacy and highly relevant to the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong system-level attribution under Xi's leadership; this is China's stated line in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The statement advocates restraint rhetorically, but does not prove implementation.
It also frames responsibility as something others, especially the U.S., must meet first.

evidence.claim: In response to the Pentagon's forecast, Zhao Lijian said China follows a self-defensive nuclear strategy, sticks to no-first-use, exercises utmost restraint, keeps capabilities at the minimum level required by national security, and is never part of any arms race.
evidence.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Zhao Lijian's Regular Press Conference on November 30, 2022
evidence.publisher: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Republic of Ireland
evidence.excerpt: In response to the Pentagon's forecast, Zhao Lijian said China follows a self-defensive nuclear strategy, sticks to no-first-use, exercises utmost restraint, keeps capabilities at the minimum level required by national security, and is never part of any arms race.
evidence.source_locator: Q&A response to AFP on the Pentagon report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Chinese government response, but it is advocacy and self-description rather than independent verification.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 contemporaneous response to the U.S. report on China's buildup.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect, but directly tied to the Xi-led state's nuclear posture claim.
contrary_evidence: This is self-justification and may understate the pace of modernization.
It does not address the 2022 silo-field buildup.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the Pentagon said China had more than 400 nuclear warheads in 2021 and could reach about 1,500 by 2035 if the current buildup pace continued, with Xi having signaled at the Party Congress that China would strengthen strategic deterrence.
evidence.title: China nuclear warhead stockpile to reach 1,500 by 2035 if it continues its build-up pace, US says
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the Pentagon said China had more than 400 nuclear warheads in 2021 and could reach about 1,500 by 2035 if the current buildup pace continued, with Xi having signaled at the Party Congress that China would strengthen strategic deterrence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong for contemporaneous reporting, though this is still secondary reporting of a Pentagon estimate.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent for late-2022 assessment of inherited and end-of-year posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; it links the build-up trend to Xi-era strategic deterrence policy.
contrary_evidence: This is a U.S. estimate, not a Chinese disclosure.
It does not by itself prove a doctrinal change away from no-first-use.

evidence.claim: FAS estimated that China's stockpile included roughly 410 nuclear warheads, with more in production, and noted that China had significantly advanced construction of its three new missile silo fields for solid-fuel ICBMs.
evidence.title: Nuclear Notebook: Chinese nuclear weapons, 2023
evidence.publisher: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists / Federation of American Scientists
evidence.excerpt: FAS estimated that China's stockpile included roughly 410 nuclear warheads, with more in production, and noted that China had significantly advanced construction of its three new missile silo fields for solid-fuel ICBMs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Widely cited technical open-source nuclear assessment from a specialist non-governmental project.
evidence.period_fit: Good retrospective fit for the 2022 end-state and the buildup underway by late 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but important for posture change under Xi's leadership.
contrary_evidence: It is an estimate, not a Chinese official count.
The notebook does not prove intended use or crisis intent.

evidence.claim: The profile says China's nuclear policy has been defined by minimum capabilities needed to deter a first strike, while also stating that China is now expanding its force through new silo fields and silos at existing fields.
evidence.title: Arms Control and Proliferation Profile: China
evidence.excerpt: The profile says China's nuclear policy has been defined by minimum capabilities needed to deter a first strike, while also stating that China is now expanding its force through new silo fields and silos at existing fields.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist arms-control summary that is explicit about both doctrine and modernization, with transparent sourcing.
evidence.period_fit: Strong inherited-baseline and end-posture context for 2022, even though the page itself is updated later.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; the doctrine is longstanding, but the expansion occurred under Xi-era leadership.
contrary_evidence: The page is updated after 2022, so it is better for context than for date-precise event chronology.
It highlights uncertainty about whether growth reflects policy change.

evidence.claim: China's export-control white paper says nuclear dual-use items, missile-related dual-use items, and related technologies are controlled through an inter-agency system involving the Ministry of Commerce, the China Atomic Energy Authority, and the CMC's equipment-development department, with expert review and compliance guidance.
evidence.title: Full Text: China's Export Controls
evidence.excerpt: China's export-control white paper says nuclear dual-use items, missile-related dual-use items, and related technologies are controlled through an inter-agency system involving the Ministry of Commerce, the China Atomic Energy Authority, and the CMC's equipment-development department, with expert review and compliance guidance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct policy white paper describing the control architecture in detail.
evidence.period_fit: Good structural fit for 2022 because the regime was already in force and still operative during the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but materially tied to Xi-era governance of dual-use risk.
contrary_evidence: This is a controls framework, not evidence of actual restraint in every sensitive domain.
It does not cover all AI/cyber/bio choices made in 2022.

evidence.claim: China halted senior-level military dialogue with the United States and cancelled a maritime military-security meeting after Pelosi's Taiwan visit, a move Reuters said raised the risk of accidental escalation at a critical moment.
evidence.title: China halts high-level military dialogue with U.S., suspends other cooperation
evidence.excerpt: China halted senior-level military dialogue with the United States and cancelled a maritime military-security meeting after Pelosi's Taiwan visit, a move Reuters said raised the risk of accidental escalation at a critical moment.
evidence.source_locator: lead and lines 418-420 in the article mirror
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is timely and specific, though republished on a financial-news site.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent fit for the August 2022 Taiwan crisis and crisis-communication lens.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Xi's system-level crisis management choice, though the press statement was issued by the foreign ministry.
contrary_evidence: Beijing framed the move as retaliation for Pelosi's visit, not as a communications risk.
The article does not show whether backchannels remained open.

evidence.claim: The white paper states that peaceful reunification is the first choice and that use of force would be the last resort under compelling circumstances.
evidence.title: Full Text: The Taiwan Question and China's Reunification in the New Era
evidence.excerpt: The white paper states that peaceful reunification is the first choice and that use of force would be the last resort under compelling circumstances.
evidence.source_locator: white paper text and the Aug. 17 press conference explanation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PRC white paper and accompanying explanation of its policy line.
evidence.period_fit: Directly contemporaneous to the August 2022 Taiwan escalation period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong; this is the policy line of the Xi-led state and party.
contrary_evidence: The same document also insists reunification cannot be halted and rejects Taiwan independence.
That combination keeps coercive risk high despite the peace-first framing.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 evidence of Xi's own assets, liabilities, outside interests, or a personal public correction/admission.
Most of the anti-corruption and data-fraud material is system-level enforcement, not proof of Xi's own candor or self-dealing.
The strongest family-wealth context is pre-2022 and indirect, so its period fit for the target year is weak.
